'''Gabriela Ines González''' (born 24 February 1965<ref>{{Cite news|url=http://www.clarin.com/sociedad/locos-Einstein-contento_0_1520848321.html|title=Estamos todos como locos... Einstein estaría muy contento|last=Losada|first=Samuel|date=2016-12-02|work=[[Clarín (Argentine newspaper)|Clarín]]|access-date=2017-12-02|language=es}}</ref>) is an Argentine professor of physics and astronomy at the [[Louisiana State University]] and was the spokesperson for the [[LIGO Scientific Collaboration]] from March 2011 until March 2017.<ref name="SU News"/>

==Biography==
Gabriela González was born on February 24, 1965, in [[Córdoba, Argentina]]. She is the daughter of Dora Trembinsky, a professor of mathematics, and Pedro González, a doctor in Economic Sciences.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |last=Serra |first=Alfredo |date=2016-02-19 |title=La doctora en Física Gabriela González, un orgullo para el país y el mundo {{!}} GENTE |url=http://www.gente.com.ar/entrevistas/la-doctora-en-fisica-gabriela-gonzalez-un-orgullo-para-el-pais-y-el-mundo/19577.html |url-status=dead |access-date=2022-10-07 |website=Gente|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160829034351/http://www.gente.com.ar/entrevistas/la-doctora-en-fisica-gabriela-gonzalez-un-orgullo-para-el-pais-y-el-mundo/19577.html |archive-date=2016-08-29 }}</ref> González completed her primary school studies at the Colegio Luterano Concordia in the city of Córdoba, and her secondary school studies at the Instituto Manuel Lucero. An avid student, González received exemplary grades at school and even had the ability to quickly solve equations in her head.<ref name=":0" />

González attended university at the [[National University of Córdoba]], which she graduated from with a Bachelor's of Science in Physics in 1988.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2016-02-14 |title=Gabriela González: "El descubrimiento merece un Premio Nobel" |url=http://www.perfil.com/ciencia/gabriela-gonzalez-el-descubrimiento-merece-un-premio-nobel-0214-0064.phtml |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161201014415/http://www.perfil.com/ciencia/gabriela-gonzalez-el-descubrimiento-merece-un-premio-nobel-0214-0064.phtml |archive-date=2016-12-01 |access-date=2022-10-07 |website=perfil.com}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Gabriela González |url=https://www.phys.lsu.edu/faculty/gonzalez/ |access-date=2022-10-07 |website=www.phys.lsu.edu}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Bär |first=Nora |date=2016-02-11 |title=Quién es Gabriela González, la argentina que confirmó la teoría de Einstein |url=https://www.lanacion.com.ar/sociedad/quien-es-gabriela-gonzalez-la-argentina-que-confirmo-la-teoria-de-einstein-nid1870117/ |access-date=2022-10-07 |website=LA NACION |language=es}}</ref> According to González, she began studying physics because she thought of it as a way to answer all of the pressing questions that humanity was faced with. In the end, however, she realized that physics does not answer all these questions but rather face us a species with more.

One year following this, she moved to the United States to study at the [[Syracuse University]], and under the tutelage of Peter Sawlson obtained her doctorate in Physics in 1995. She began a postdoc at [[Massachusetts Institute of Technology|MIT]], where she later worked as a researcher, and then after that as a professor at [[Pennsylvania State University]]. Beginning in April 2001, she began working as a professor at Louisiana State University.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Gabriela González Curriculum Vitae |url=https://www.phys.lsu.edu/faculty/gonzalez/CV.pdf |access-date=2022-10-07 |website=Louisiana State University}}</ref>

In 2008, González became the first woman to receive a full professorship in the Department of Physics and Astronomy at Louisiana State University.<ref>{{Cite journal |date=2016-12-01 |title=Nature's 10 |journal=Nature |language=en |volume=540 |issue=7634 |pages=507–515 |doi=10.1038/540507a |pmid=30905952 |bibcode=2016Natur.540..507. |s2cid=49905540 |issn=1476-4687|doi-access=free }}</ref>

González believes that science will be much better off when there are as many women as men, and that this will happens when the common myths and misconceptions about physicists, which tend to segregate women from research, start to fall apart, and furthermore when people believe that physicists are simply normal people with normal lives.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Domínguez |first=Nuño |date=2018-08-20 |title="La ciencia irá mucho mejor cuando tengamos tantas mujeres como hombres" |language=es |work=El País |url=https://elpais.com/elpais/2018/07/10/ciencia/1531239620_454388.html |access-date=2022-10-07 |issn=1134-6582}}</ref>

Before moving to the United States, González began a relationship with [[Jorge Pullin]], an Argentinian theoretical physicist with specializations in black hole collisions and the theory of [[quantum gravity]] working at Louisiana State University. They later wed. The two have no children.

==Career==
González has published several papers on [[Brownian motion]] as a limit to the sensitivity of [[gravitational-wave detector]]s, and has an interest in data analysis for [[gravitational-wave astronomy]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Gabriela González, PhD|url=http://www.phys.lsu.edu/newwebsite/people/gonzalez.html|publisher=[[Louisiana State University]]|access-date=5 May 2014|archive-date=16 May 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160516192535/http://www.phys.lsu.edu/newwebsite/people/gonzalez.html|url-status=dead}}</ref>

In February 2016, she was one of five [[LIGO]] scientists present for the announcement that the first direct [[gravitational wave observation]] had been detected in September 2015.<ref>{{Cite news|title = Gravitational Waves Exist: The Inside Story of How Scientists Finally Found Them|url = http://www.newyorker.com/tech/elements/gravitational-waves-exist-heres-how-scientists-finally-found-them|newspaper = [[The New Yorker]]|access-date = 2016-02-11|issn = 0028-792X|first = Nicola|last = Twilley}}</ref><ref name="PRL-20160211">{{cite journal |author=Abbott, B.P. |title=Observation of Gravitational Waves from a Binary Black Hole Merger |journal=[[Phys. Rev. Lett.]] |volume=116 |issue=6 |article-number=061102 |year=2016 |doi=10.1103/PhysRevLett.116.061102 |display-authors=etal |pmid=26918975|arxiv=1602.03837 |bibcode=2016PhRvL.116f1102A |s2cid=119286014 }}</ref><ref name="Naeye">{{cite news |last=Naeye |first=Robert |url=http://www.skyandtelescope.com/astronomy-news/gravitational-wave-detection-heralds-new-era-of-science-0211201644/ |title=Gravitational Wave Detection Heralds New Era of Science |work=[[Sky and Telescope]] |date=11 February 2016 |access-date=11 February 2016 }}</ref><ref name="Nature_11Feb16">{{cite journal |title=Einstein's gravitational waves found at last |journal=[[Nature News]]|url=http://www.nature.com/news/einstein-s-gravitational-waves-found-at-last-1.19361 |date=11 February 2016 |last1=Castelvecchi |first1=Davide |last2=Witze |first2=Alexandra |doi=10.1038/nature.2016.19361 |s2cid=182916902|access-date=11 February 2016 |url-access=subscription |doi-access=free }}</ref>{{efn|Other physicists present for the announcement were [[David Reitze]], [[Rainer Weiss]], [[Kip Thorne]], and [[France A. Córdova]].}}
She was a staff scientist in the LIGO group at MIT, joined the faculty at Penn State in 1997 and moved to LSU in 2001.
<ref>{{cite web |url=https://perimeterinstitute.ca/people/gabriela-gonzalez |title=Gabriela Gonzalez &#124; Perimeter Institute }}</ref>
In 2024, González was elected as the vice-president of the [[American Physical Society]], having been a fellow since 2007.<ref>{{Cite web |title=LSU Boyd Professor Elected Vice President of American Physical Society |url=https://www.lsu.edu/physics/news/2024/gonzalez_vp_aps.php |access-date=2025-02-10 |website=www.lsu.edu}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=2024-11-09 |title=APS General Election Results {{!}} American Physical Society |url=https://www.aps.org/about/governance/general-election |access-date=2025-02-10 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20241109194041/https://www.aps.org/about/governance/general-election |archive-date=9 November 2024 }}</ref>

==Awards==
González was elected fellow of the [[Institute of Physics]] (2004), the [[American Physical Society]] (2007), and the [[American Astronomical Society]] (2020).<ref>{{cite web|url=https://aas.org/grants-and-prizes/aas-fellows|title=AAS Fellows|publisher=AAS|access-date=28 September 2020}}</ref>

She won the [[American Physical Society#Edward A. Bouchet Award|Bouchet Award]] in 2007, the [[Bruno Rossi Prize]] in 2017, the [[National Academy of Sciences]] Award for Scientific Discovery in 2017, and the [[Petrie Prize Lecture]] in 2019.<ref>{{cite web|title=Award for Scientific Discovery|url=http://www.nasonline.org/programs/awards/2017/Gonzaelz-Reitze-Saulson.html|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170130211258/http://www.nasonline.org/programs/awards/2017/Gonzaelz-Reitze-Saulson.html|url-status=dead|archive-date=January 30, 2017|publisher=[[National Academy of Sciences]]|access-date=11 March 2017}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|title=Edward A. Bouchet Award|url=http://www.aps.org/programs/honors/awards/bouchet.cfm|publisher=[[American Physical Society]]|access-date=5 May 2014}}</ref>

González was elected to membership in the National Academy of Sciences and the [[American Academy of Arts and Sciences]] in 2017.<ref>{{cite web |title=National Academy of Sciences Members and Foreign Associates Elected |publisher=National Academy of Sciences |date=May 2, 2017 |url=http://www.nasonline.org/news-and-multimedia/news/may-2-2017-NAS-Election.html|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170503160816/http://www.nasonline.org/news-and-multimedia/news/may-2-2017-NAS-Election.html|url-status=dead|archive-date=May 3, 2017}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |last1=Satake |first1=Alison |title=LSU's Gabriela González Elected to the American Academy of Arts and Sciences |url=https://www.lsu.edu/mediacenter/news/2017/04/12physastro_gonzalez_academy.php |access-date=2 May 2021 |work=LSU Media Center |date=April 12, 2017}}</ref>

==Personal life==
González is married to [[Jorge Pullin]], the [[Horace Hearne Institute|Horace Hearne Chair]] in theoretical Physics at the [[Louisiana State University]].<ref name="SU News">{{cite news |last1=Enslin |first1=Rob |title=Physicist Gabriela González G'95 Reveals How Syracuse Prepared Her to Make Science History |url=https://news.syr.edu/blog/2019/01/04/physicist-gabriela-gonzalez-g95-reveals-how-syracuse-prepared-her-to-make-science-history/ |access-date=2 May 2021 |work=SU News |date=January 4, 2019}}</ref>
